question.text: Sodium light of wavelengths <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>650</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>655</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> is used to study diffraction at a single slit of aperture <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The distance between the slit and the screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The separation between the positions of the first maxima of diffraction pattern obtained in the two cases is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>

solution.text:
The condition for maxima in diffraction is,

bsinθ=2n+1λ2.

 For the first maxima n=1. Therefore,

bsinθ=3λ2⇒sinθ=3λ2b=yDy=3λD2b

Now the difference between the positions of the maxima will be,

y1-y2=3D2bλ1-λ2⇒y1-y2=3×22×5×10-4×655-650×10-9=3×10-5 m
